summary: Robert L. Brown was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He served as a curator of South and Southeast Asian art at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1980–2014) and professor at UCLA (~1986–2014).

Robert Lenz studied at the University of Tartu and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp. He held posts at Tallinn Cathedral School, University of Breslau, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and Saint Petersburg State University as professor of Sanskrit (~1835–1836).

Robert M. Gimello was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from Columbia University (~1968–1976). He served on the faculty at the University of Arizona (~1981–1998) and Harvard University (~2001–2007).

Robert Maclagan worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and Royal School of Military Engineering, and served as principal of IIT Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

Robert Magliola is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Princeton (~1965–1970). He held faculty posts at Purdue (1969), Tamkang, Assumption University, and National Taiwan University (1987–1998).

Robert Mayer specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Bristol and Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen, and joined the Oriental Studies faculty at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Robert Needham Cust worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Eton, Trinity College Cambridge, East India Company College, Haileybury, and Fort William College, later serving in the Bengal Civil Service from approximately 1843 to 1867.

Robert P. Goldman is an Indologist who studied at Columbia and the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher, Shivram Dattatray Joshi, and T. S. Srinivasa Sastri. He spent his career at UC Berkeley (~1971–2021), becoming professor emeritus in 2021.

Robert P. Scharlemann was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Concordia College, Concordia Seminary, and Heidelberg University. He held faculty posts at the University of Southern California (~1965–1966), University of Iowa (~1966–1981), and University of Virginia (~1981–2004).

Robert S. Ellwood was a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Colorado, Yale University, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, and served on the faculty at the University of Southern California (~1967–1997).

Robert S. Nelson is an art historian and archaeologist who studied at Rice University and New York University. He held professorships at the University of Chicago (~1974–2005) and Yale University (~2005–2021).
Robert S. P. Beekes was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Leiden University under F. B. J. Kuiper, taught at Marnix Gymnasium, and held posts at Leiden University in 1973 and 1979.
Robert Sewell was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1868–1894) and held a post as Keeper of the Tamil Nadu Archives.
Robert Seymour Conway was a linguist who studied at the City of London School (~1877–1883). He held academic posts at Newnham College (~1887–1893) and Gonville and Caius College (~1888–1894).

Robert Warren Clark is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Karen Christina Lang and studied under adviser and teacher K. L. Seshagiri Rao (attested 1994).

Robert Zimmermann was an Indologist who studied at St Beuno's and Humboldt University of Berlin (1908–1913). He served as professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930) and led the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Robert Zydenbos is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies who studied at Utrecht University (~1975–1983). He held posts at the University of Toronto, University of Munich (~2003), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).
Robert van Gulik was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (~1929–1934) and at Utrecht University (~1934–1935) under doctoral supervisor Jan Gonda.

Robin Coningham is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at King's College and the University of Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin. He held posts at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (appointed 2005).
Robin D. S. Yates is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~1975–1980) and held a James McGill Professorship at McGill University (~1993).
